english: Let $R=\left\{(x,y)\in\mathbb{R}^{2}:[x]^{2}\le y\le 3-2[x]\right\}$, where $[t]$ denotes the greatest integer less than or equal to $t$. The line $x=\lambda$ divides $R$ into two parts of equal area. Then the value of $\lambda$ is ______.
hindi: माना कि $R=\left\{(x,y)\in\mathbb{R}^{2}:[x]^{2}\le y\le 3-2[x]\right\}$ है, जहाँ $[t]$, $t$ से छोटा या उसके बराबर महत्तम पूर्णांक है। रेखा $x=\lambda$, $R$ को समान क्षेत्रफल वाले दो भागों में विभाजित करती है। तब $\lambda$ का मान ______ है।
solution: On $[n,n+1)$, $[x]=n$ and the vertical section is $n^{2}\le y\le 3-2n$, non-empty iff $n^{2}+2n-3\le 0\Leftrightarrow -3\le n\le 1$, i.e. $x\in[-3,2)$.
Heights $3-2n-n^{2}=4-(n+1)^{2}$: $n=-3,-2,-1,0,1$ give $0,3,4,3,0$. So $R$ is (up to segments of zero area) three rectangles over $[-2,1)$, total area $10$.
Area to the left of $x=\lambda$ equals $5$: $3+4(\lambda+1)=5\Rightarrow\lambda=-\dfrac12$ (the heights are symmetric about $x=-\frac12$).
solution_full: Fix $x$ with $[x]=n$, i.e. $n\le x<n+1$. The points of $R$ above $x$ are $n^{2}\le y\le 3-2n$. This is non-empty iff $n^{2}\le 3-2n$, i.e. $n^{2}+2n-3\le 0$, $(n+3)(n-1)\le 0$, $-3\le n\le 1$. So the $x$-values of $R$ are $[-3,2)$, exactly as for the domain of $\sqrt{3-2[x]-[x]^{2}}$.

For $n=-3$ and $n=1$ the sections are single points ($y=9$ and $y=1$), giving segments of zero area. So $R$ consists, up to area zero, of the rectangles $[-2,-1)\times[4,7]$, $[-1,0)\times[1,5]$ and $[0,1)\times[0,3]$, with areas $3,4,3$; total $10$.

The left area as a function of $\lambda$ increases from $0$ to $10$ as $\lambda$ goes from $-2$ to $1$, strictly on $[-2,1]$. After $[-2,-1)$ it is $3<5$; after $[-1,0)$ it is $7>5$, so $-1<\lambda<0$ and $3+4(\lambda+1)=5$, $\lambda=-\dfrac12$.
This agrees with the symmetry of the heights $3,4,3$ about the midpoint $x=-\dfrac12$ of $[-2,1]$.
originality_note: New: a region between two step curves y = [x]^2 and y = 3 - 2[x], whose x-range is found exactly like the domain of a GIF function, and whose heights 4 - (n+1)^2 are symmetric so the bisector is x = -1/2 (way 4, hidden symmetry). Closest known: area under y = [x] or a bisecting line of a region. Different because: the region is given only by a double inequality in [x], two of its columns degenerate to segments, and the bisector comes from the symmetric heights.

concept_use.Areas involving GIF, fractional part or: R is a union of rectangles of heights 3, 4, 3 on unit intervals; the bisecting line is found from these areas.
concept_use.Domain and range of functions involving: The x-range of R is found by solving [x]^2 + 2[x] - 3 <= 0, as for the domain of sqrt(3 - 2[x] - [x]^2): [x] in {-3,...,1}, x in [-3,2).
